The NATO issue was raised at the Coalition of the Willing in Berlin. The Allies understand that the clearest security guarantee for Ukraine is NATO membership. And the clearest way to strengthen NATO is to bring Ukraine in. This works for both sides: Ukraine and NATO.

As for NATO Article 5-like security guarantees: Article 5 is about collective defense. For Ukraine, it's not clear yet, because we still don't have a full answer about what this collective would be, how it would defend us, and whether it would be ready to repel the aggressor. But if we have something “Article 5-like,” then there are a lot of questions about this “like.” The answers should not just be words – this has to be on paper.

We have to guarantee Ukraine, our citizens first and foremost, and all of Europe that security guarantees for Ukraine will be strong not only for these two years while President Trump is the President of the United States, but beyond that as well. We're fighting to defend our country not just for two years. And we need security guarantees not for two years, but forever. Even if Putin and Trump are friends, as it turned out recently, the idea that Putin might be afraid to do something, to launch another aggression for two years only, does not work for us. That's not a strong peace. That's a two-year pause.

From answers to journalists’ questions. (1/3)

Microsoft has filed a patent application for AI that can rewrite what people say during livestreams in near real time and change their lip movements to match.

The system would flag words based on preset rules or a viewer’s profile, such as age, language or location. Generative AI would then replace or remove those words, smooth the audio and change the speaker’s mouth and facial movements so the edit is seamless. Examples in the filing include live translation, cutting filler words and stutters, fixing mispronunciations, removing profanity and adapting content for different age groups or regions.

The filing says the original unedited stream would be kept as a “ground truth” record. Microsoft hasn’t said whether it plans to build the product.

Billionaire investor Howard Marks says the speed of AI progress is a risk for Anthropic and OpenAI.

“Perhaps the most startling characteristic of AI is the speed at which it makes progress,” the Oaktree Capital cofounder wrote in a new memo, “A Layman Thinks About AI.” Since OpenAI and Anthropic quickly overtook earlier players, he asked, “can they likewise be supplanted by others, or at least challenged?”

Marks warned that “it takes a lot to maintain a lead in a rapidly changing technology.” He noted that hyperscalers like Microsoft, Amazon and Alphabet can build competing tools, which makes the labs hard to value. “If the competitive picture can shift as I suggest, how much is a stake in today’s leaders worth?”
